##### Please mark this post as secret, as it's a secret meeting in the forest.

A slip of a girl, ran through the forest, giggling unto herself. Primrose a bloom, surrounded her, like corridors of poisonous colour. Guiding her whippet feet, to a far off destination. The soft dew licked grass, tickling her toes as she ran. The scent of the morning, the earth and the grass, filled her with exuberance. A new day, a new dawn. Prophetic thoughts overwhelmed her, and renewed her vigour. As she ran, a light wisp on two feet, a rich voice touched her ears. A deep, soft counting grew louder.. Six.... Five... She slowed to a walk, a beautiful gait to delight the eyes. She passed him there in the woods, still counting.. Her arm reached out, and her hand touched his. A secret meeting of the minds, her thoughts touched his. They were one for a moment, God and Goddess, unified in mind and purpose.

'It's so sad about the Illithid' she thought. 'So few in number, so large in appetite. They cannot feast upon the Saen forever'.

'What to do' his mind answered back.

'I have a planet sized brain to feed them' her mind replied.

'But ice cannot sustain them', he questioned back

'But the parasite that feeds upon the ice can, filled with its own new thoughts. Ten legions, says you cannot rescue them' She goaded

'Fine' he answered. His thoughts becoming bored.

Her fingertips slid from his embrace, their thoughts became their own. [Two lonely ships, continued their journey, a distance betwixt them](http://ultraimg.com/images/imaged8a02.jpg). One of them counting, bored and uninterested, as if nothing had happened. The other, with a smile upon her lips.

The girl, stepped off the paths, and onto a crossroads. She changed from a beauty, into a horrible old hag, pushing a cart. The old hag followed the road, into the Roost. There in the market, he found a trader. An enterprising young Thorac, selling magical flowers. He picked out the best, the ones that would work, and left the trader, with a smile on his face.

---

In a dark forest, on the back of a beast, that lay in the cold, on a world it consumed, a little girl fed her pet, smelly little [flowers](http://ultraimg.com/images/imageb139a.jpg).

As the girl scampered away, Cruxius hid his smile. So capricious that one, yet endearing. He chuckled softly to himself and smiled as he threw 2 berries in the air, catching the first in his upturned mouth, but missing the second. As he leaned over to grab the other from the ground, he grabbed some of the dirt and let it run between his fingers. The Crossroads was a lonely place when the land itself wasn't squirming to greet you. He stepped off the grass and onto the golden paving stones of the Hecate Road. Lazily he strode towards a crossing with a signpost that listed names of places, some of which had yet to know their own name, but here there was only one that interested him: "Pome's Sanctuary --->". He thought briefly of Vakni, and shortly after a portal opened before him. Vakni stepped through the portal and into the Crossroads, still with her nose stuffed in that book. "Anything interesting?"

"Mostly incantations and rituals for the worship of Godric, my lord," Vakni replied. "Something about 'moon magic' here and there scattered about, and information on the Moon gates, of course, but nothing I'm sure you didn't know already, and certainly nothing worth wasting my time poring over."

Cruxius smiled again. She was short with him, as always, and rather than find it grating, he found it amusing. Her and Iskandar both, so insolent, even before a god. Perhaps I should be more imposing, but, alas, I cannot help myself. I never was much one for heavy-handedness. "If the book bores you so then I will offer you another task. There are creatures in Pome's Sanctuary known as Illithid. Various shapes and sizes, I'm sure, as they reproduce by devouring the brain of a host and taking over its body. I want you to go there and ask Pome what he wants for them. If he asks, I have offered them shelter. Let him know that I intend to assist them in repopulating their species, and may even help them find their precious city, Spalix, if they so desire. Long ago they were a great people and served VeussueV well, but he has long since abandoned them. You are to bring the Illithid here, and having done that..." Cruxius plucked one of the blooming primrose flowers from a nearby tree and dipped it in his chalice. When it came free from the liquid, the flower now shone iridescently, purple trailing into gold in the light. "...You will consume this primrose. Zille will take this as a sign that your task is completed and will fetch you from there. I'm not sure what her plans are, exactly, but see what you can find out from wherever she takes you." Cruxius handed Vakni the iridescent blossom, and took the book from her hands. "This, on the other hand...this I will have to find something to do with. It appears Godric recovered and ran off without it. Be on now, and return to me when you have news."

Vakni bowed deeply, so deeply that Cruxisu was almost certain she was mocking him. "As you wish, Lord Cruxius." She produced the key, Sleipnir, from her coat, inserted it into the sign post beside the sign for Pome's Sanctuary, and turned. A portal opened beside her and she stepped through onto the lush shores of a paradise...

Marching back down that path as he read from the Book of the Moon, Cruxius came finally to a signpost that read "<--- The Free City of Sentenza" and took another sip from his chalice. He waved his hand and another portal appeared, this time to the Hall of the Moon in Sentenza.

Cruxius arrived in what appeared to be an office, though perhaps, judging by the size and the equipment, it was more of a private laboratory than just an office. A Spectre, golden as the Hecate Road, 'stood' behind a desk riffling through papers of equations and diagrams. Quadrivus, engulfed in his experiments, didn't notice his entrance at first, assuming him to be another wandered come to ask for his assistance in some task or another. "Yes, what is it? What do you want then?" he asked harshly. "We're terribly busy right now and I haven't got much time for..." He gazed up finally and saw Cruxius, who was hiding his smirk behind his chalice once again. "Lord Cruxius!" he gasped. He attempted a bow, as much as the Spectra could attempt such a corporeal gesture, and began babbling apologies like a madman.

"That is enough Quadrivus. I see you are busy and I would not disturb your work, for you may have need of it soon. I come offering a new avenue of research, however, one that might yet augment your labors." Cruxius pulled the book from under his arm and placed it on the desk beside the Spectre's notes. "You see before you a holy artifact of Godric, god of the moons. Contained within is knowledge of his works, rites, and possibly more, but most importantly are the notes concerning the Cathedral Luna and the magic of the moons. Do with it as you will, but make haste, for surely Godric will seek it soon. For now, I will take my leave of you." A portal once again opened behind him and he stepped through. Before it closed he stopped and turned once more. "Oh, and Quadrivus, do give my best to Iskandar. I can feel from here he has no wish to see me, but the day may come soon when he may yet seek my favour. Farewell." With that, the portal vanished before Quadrivus' eyes.

Quadrivus reached out to grasp the Book before him, and as his form grazed the binding an intense pain seared through him. Where his form had brushed the Book, had simply ceased to be, just as if he were in direct moonlight. Such an artifact would be anathema to the Spectra. Why in Gaea's name had Cruxius given it to him? For now, he reasoned, the Book would be his priority, but where to begin...
